channel.title: Ghent Screens
channel.description: Daily screenings at Ghent's arthouse cinemas and film clubs, rarest films first, with who paid for each film. Kinepolis not included.

item.title: Ghent screens · Sunday 25 October · 23 films
item.description:
1. KIDScinema: The Best of Filem'On (1× this week): KASKcinema 10:30
    Funding: Short films for children from the Filem'On festival. Funding is not tracked for mixed programmes.
  2. Yugly (1× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00
    Funding: Brussels animation studio nWave made it with Octopolis. The Belgian tax shelter, raised through Umedia, and screen.brussels helped pay for it. Shown as Mochy in French.
  3. Yugly NV (1× this week): Sphinx 11:00
  4. Monster Mia (1× this week): Sphinx 14:30
  5. Minotaur (1× this week): Studio Skoop 17:00
    Funding: A French-German-Latvian co-production led by MK Productions and CG Cinema, with Forma Pro Films, Razor Film and ARTE France Cinéma. mk2 Films sells it and Les Films du Losange distributes it; France picked it as its Oscar entry.
  6. Erfgoedlezing Pacificatie van Gent (1× this week): Liberas time on site
  7. The Odyssey - (2× this week): Studio Skoop 16:30
  8. Coyote vs. Acme (2× this week): Sphinx 20:30
  9. Tegenwoordig heet iedereen sorry (3× this week): Sphinx 11:00; Studio Skoop 14:00
    Funding: A Flemish youth film produced by Ivy Vanhaecke at deMENSEN, with Germany's CALA Filmproduktion and Juliet at Pupkin. LevelK sells it abroad. The listing we found names no public funds.
  10. The Last One for the Road (Andiamo a bere l'ultima) (3× this week): Sphinx 14:30
  11. Please, Open the Curtains (3× this week): NTGent 15:00
  12. Notre salut (3× this week): Sphinx 17:00
    Funding: A Franco-Belgian co-production by Kidam and Brussels-based Michigan Films, made for under €5 million. Co-producers include France 2 Cinéma, Belgium's public broadcaster RTBF and Be tv/Proximus, and the CNC gave an advance on receipts plus development and distribution aid.
  13. The Return (2003) (4× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00
    Funding: Zvyagintsev's debut was produced by REN Film, the Moscow company of Dmitry Lesnevsky. Shown alongside his new film Minotaur.
  14. La Gradiva (5× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00
  15. Naza (5× this week): Sphinx 11:00 · 20:30
    Funding: A documentary from the No Other Land team, produced by James Wilson's JW Films with The Guardian, in association with Placeholder Films and Unseen Hand. Jonathan Glazer is an executive producer and mk2 Films handles world sales.
  16. Franz (7× this week): Studio Skoop 17:00
    Funding: A Kafka biopic stitched together from many public sources. Marlene Film (Prague), X Filme (Berlin) and Metro Films (Warsaw) produced it, joined by Czech, Polish and German broadcasters and Canal+. Funding came from Eurimages, the Czech Audiovisual Fund, the Polish Film Institute, Medienboard Berlin-Brandenburg and Germany's DFFF.
  17. Shaun Het Schaap: Het Beest van de Boerderij (9× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00 · 14:30 · 17:00; Sphinx 11:00 · 14:30
  18. Sense and Sensibility (9× this week): Studio Skoop 14:15; Sphinx 17:15
    Funding: Working Title Films produced it with November Pictures and Kiddo Films. Working Title belongs to Universal, which releases the film internationally while its arthouse label Focus Features handles the US.
  19. Digger (10× this week): Sphinx 17:15; Studio Skoop 20:00
    Funding: A Hollywood studio picture: Legendary Pictures produced it in partnership with Warner Bros., which also distributes it. Tom Cruise is a producer alongside Iñárritu and Mary Parent. Warner Bros. says the budget stayed at $125 million; reports of $160–180 million were denied by the studio.
  20. Primetime (10× this week): Sphinx 17:30; Studio Skoop 20:00
    Funding: A24 both finances and distributes this one. Robert Pattinson produces through his company Icki Eneo Arlo, with Range Media Partners and Square Peg also credited. No budget has been published.
  21. The Invite (15× this week): Sphinx 14:30 · 20:30; Studio Skoop 20:00
    Funding: Produced by Megan Ellison's Annapurna, then sold at Sundance 2026. A24 won a days-long bidding war against Focus Features and paid more than $12 million for the rights.
  22. Wicker (16× this week): Studio Skoop 14:00 · 20:00; Sphinx 14:30 · 20:30
    Funding: Financed by Tango and Topic Studios, with development money from Votiv; South of The River and Yoki also produce. Black Bear bought it at Sundance 2026 for North America and the UK and handles international sales.
  23. Coward (40× this week): Studio Skoop 11:00 · 14:30 · 17:00 · 19:45; Sphinx 11:00 · 17:30 · 20:30
    Funding: Lukas Dhont's third feature is led by his Belgian company The Reunion, with Lumen (France), Topkapi Films (Netherlands) and Versus (Belgium) as co-producers. Brussels' regional fund put in €125,000, which it lists as about 1.2% of the budget, so the film cost roughly €10 million. The Match Factory sells it abroad and Diaphana releases it in France.
